title: Reduce CPU context switches and message copying with ringbuffer serializer and batch coalescer
author: Priya Nambiar
description:
Motivation: CPU-side overhead on the request path has been the dominant cost for short requests in our hosted service. Profiling across multiple workloads (chat, short-completion, and embeddings) shows excessive context switches, frequent small allocations during request serialization, and lock contention in the per-GPU worker pool. This PR introduces a compact ring-buffer based serializer + a lightweight batch coalescer to: (1) avoid copying small message frames across thread boundaries, (2) reduce futex wakeups by aggregating send events, and (3) make continuous batching cheaper for high-qps short requests. The change is intentionally incremental and guarded behind a runtime flag for easy rollback.

Design summary: a lock-free single-producer-multi-consumer ring buffer sits between request acceptors (IO threads) and per-worker executors. Small serialized frames are placed into the ring buffer with a fast path that avoids heap allocations and avoids taking the worker pool mutex on the hot path. Workers poll the ring buffer and coalesce adjacent frames into a single outbound batch when the combined size is under a configurable coalesce_window (default 5120 bytes / 2ms). The serializer reserves contiguous ranges in the ring to allow zero-copy writes; when a frame crosses the end, it uses a short two-fragment header to avoid an extra copy. The worker-side dequeue is wait-free for typical cases (backpressure uses a lightweight backoff) and only falls back to the main executor queue when the ring is full.

KV-cache and scheduling interaction: the ring buffer exposes per-request metadata flags so worker executors can prefetch KV entries before deserialization of the prompt body. We also tuned the executor scheduler to prefer local dequeue and to delay thread yields for a small adaptive window when high throughput is detected. That reduces context switching between IO threads and worker threads under steady load.

Implementation highlights: runtime/transport/ring_serializer.h/.cc (new), runtime/worker_pool/batch_coalescer.cc (new), runtime/scheduler tweaks to prefer local work-stealing avoidance, runtime/tests/ring_serializer_test.cc (unit), perf/bench/ring_coalesce_bench.cc (microbench). Small API additions: TransportFrame header contains coalesce_hint and kv_prefetch_hint bits. The runtime flag `--enable-ring-serializer` defaults to off in production until canary runs complete.

Benchmarks: representative end-to-end perf harness (chat-short template): p50 latency reduced from 18.4ms -> 12.2ms (-33.7%), p95 68ms -> 45ms (-33.8%), p99 156ms -> 97ms (-37.8%). CPU per-request cycles (measured via perf and taskstats) decreased ~28% on average. Tail throughput improved ~+22% in the continuous-batching scenario. Memory allocator churn (malloc/free counts) for the hot path dropped by ~90% in microbench runs.

Testing & rollout: added unit tests and integration tests. Perf harness scripts included to reproduce numbers. Canary rollout plan: enable flag in dedicated canary pool for 48 hours; monitor p99 latency, CPU utilization, and trace sampling (we added a trace tag to indicate ring-serializer path). Early canary on staging shows stable improvements without new errors.

Checklist:
- [x] unit tests
- [x] integration tests
- [x] perf bench harness
- [x] canary plan documented
- [x] telemetry (metric: runtime.ring_serializer.coalesced_bytes, coalesce_batches, ring_contention)

Related: ENG-1289 (request path CPU optimizations), ENG-1297 (continuous batching improvements). See design note: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1289/ringbuffer-serializer-design for rationale.

review_comments: Diego: Can you explain failure modes when ring buffer is full? Is there a fallback to existing path?

Author (Priya): Yes — when ring is full we fall back to enqueueing on the existing worker mutex-protected queue. That path preserves correctness and is documented in the code. We added metrics to track fallbacks.
Anya: Please reduce the default coalesce window; 10ms felt long for low-latency callers.
Author (Priya): lowered default to 2ms and added dynamic tuning based on request size histogram. Also added an env var for per-deployment override.
Marcus: CI failed on clang-tidy; some header includes were duplicated.
Author (Priya): fixed include order, pushed patch, re-ran CI — all green now.

test_instructions: Run runtime/tests/ring_serializer_test.cc and perf/bench/ring_coalesce_bench.cc. To reproduce e2e, enable --enable-ring-serializer in a canary dedicated pool and run perf/harness/chat-short.sh
